title: Angkor Wat
visualBrief: Complete ancient Angkor Wat architectural ensemble: native three concentric galleries/open courts, five articulated lotus-bud towers, curved corbelled stone roofs, real gallery openings/colonnade and turned balusters, layered plinths/steep steps, six libraries and cruciform galleries, full outer laterite enclosure/four gateways, monumental west gopura and ancient causeway/naga rails. Exact native master plans with photographically estimated sections/repeats and simplified far levels; no natural moat/forest/site slab or later separate monastery/stupa.

geographicProposal.notes: Complete Angkor Wat ancient architectural ensemble: five central lotus-bud towers and their tiered sanctuaries; three concentric galleries with native open courts, cruciform connecting galleries, six mapped libraries, bounded intrinsic terraces/stone stairs/paved causeways and naga balustrades; west monumental gopura plus north/east/south outer gates and full native enclosure wall network. Include ancient western bridge/causeway footprint. No natural moat/water/forest/landscape mesh or entire82ha ground slab; modern floating pontoon/access facilities, later separate stupa/monasteries/sculpture collections, neighboring Angkor monuments and people excluded.

limitations: Exact original OSM area payload establishes three gallery multipolygons/courtyard holes, fifty explicit-height roof/tower parts and five tower footprint controls, six library footprints, cruciform galleries/Terrace of Honor, four outer gateways, four enclosure wall polylines and the ancient west causeway polygon. Original coordinates retained in source/map controls; native heights and note="simplified shape" are mapped estimates, not survey accuracy. Roof sections, stone steps/courses/colonnade and baluster/window repeats, lost gate fragments and concealed details are photographic medium-fi interpretations. Far LODs simplify small plan articulations while retaining all defining structures.

Upper entry/corner pavilion sections are bounded Boolean intersections of original native gallery polygons and explicit estimated16m selection boxes. Ground master footprint/courtyard topology remains native; exact upper pavilion/pediment/roof breakage and concealed details remain original photographic medium-fi interpretations, not independent surveyed pavilion footprints.

All ancient structures in scope are retained, including six mapped libraries, cruciform galleries, ancient west causeway, four outer gateways and full enclosure wall polylines. The present conservation state of concealed N/S/E gateway wings is conservatively represented by broken walls/lintels, not complete invented roofs. Separate later Chedei Chey Non stupa, modern monasteries/floating bridge/access facilities and neighboring temples are excluded.

Mapped native roof/tower heights are simplified estimates. Gallery platform/court levels4/11/23m, six library floor sections, vaulted profiles, tier taper/lotus finials, plinth/door/pediment details, stone/baluster/column counts, naga anatomy and exact stair landings remain photographic medium-fi estimates. Native master footprints/courtyard topology are retained; distant levels simplify small projections and roof sections. Individual ancient sculpture/epic relief figures are original representative motifs, not an exact census or photograph texture.
